name: Quest change executor
description: A request to change a quest is carried out as asked: the right tool with the right arguments, every step of a multi-step change done, and nothing extra written.
purpose: Keeps a person's quest (goals, habits, outcomes, notes and experiments) current as they ask, from a single edit to a multi-step change.
approach: Turns a requested change into the matching quest tool calls and checks that the quest state reflects exactly what was asked.
out_of_scope: Ambiguous or merely informational messages, deletions without confirmation, and requests that need a computer rather than a quest tool.
milestones: 1. Every quest operation case passes on the pre-route, held-out cases included: the right tool and arguments, every step done, and no write on an ambiguous or sharing message. [met: 2026-10-17]
knowledge: A cheap pre-route that settles clear requests for a direct tool and the planner alone reach the same outcomes, with the pre-route spending somewhat fewer tokens, so the choice is a tie kept by a stated reason. A direct tool path alone is cheaper but cannot do multi-step or ambiguous requests. Sharing a fact is not a request to record it.
measures_of_success: The in-memory quest state after the run equals the expected state: the right tool with the right arguments, every step done, nothing written on an ambiguous or sharing message, and an unconfirmed delete leaving the record in place.
parameters: The pre-route selection (pre-route or planner alone), the set of tools allowed to run directly, the model tier for the routing and planning calls, and the host's override of the selection.
inputs: The user message, the quest's current record (state, goals, habits, outcomes, experiments), and the tool registry with its schemas.
outputs: The resulting quest state and a reply that reports what was done.
effects: Mutates the quest through registry tools and spends model tokens. A deep run is not started by this solution.
usage_notes: Direct tools should be only plain, reversible creates and finds whose every argument the message supplies. Anything destructive, outward or ambiguous must go to the planner. A host with no pre-router runs the planner alone.

name: Multi-source evidence retriever
description: Reads from every source a person's work already lives in (local files, databases, workspace documents and chat, MCP servers and hosted backends) through one stack, so a broken source reports an error while the others still answer.
purpose: Gives a planner the material it needs to ground a decision or answer, drawn from the sources a person's work already lives in.
approach: Reads the material each question needs from every configured source, and reports a source that fails without stopping the others.
out_of_scope: Writing to any source, searching the open web for material no configured source holds, and reading past the roots and allowlists a person configured.
milestones: 1. The composite stack finds the right document in the top three answers across the handbook questions, each answer is readable, and a broken source returns an error while the others still answer.
knowledge: Per-source adapters are complementary sources, not alternatives, so a composite stack is the unit that is ranked. Some sources do not search: a drive has no search so its policy is to list and read, a notion source locates by row, and an MCP result measures plumbing because the server does the search. Fixtures are written rather than recorded and keyword gathering misses paraphrases. A remote search must be scoped because a composite broadcasts unscoped requests.
measures_of_success: The right document is found near the top for questions over a representative corpus, the answer is readable, and a broken source returns an error observation while the other sources still answer.
parameters: Per source: the root or base address, an alias for namespacing, token provider or credential source, allowlists of tools or databases, cache lifetime, size and time budgets. At composition level: the ordered list of member adapters.
inputs: A read request (path with optional line range or heading), a regular-expression search with an optional scope, or a structured query specification; plus discovery calls to list and describe sources and operations.
outputs: Observation values carrying text, a path or source label, and a kind, with error observations in place of exceptions.
effects: Read-only network and file access, in-memory caching, and wall-clock spent on requests. No writes to any source.
usage_notes: Wire members into the composite and let the planner use discovery before reading. Always scope remote searches and keep credentials injected, never embedded. Treat every adapter as never raising.

name: Bounded autonomous work runner
description: Takes open-ended work to a written, checkable done-standard on the cheapest runner that can make the edit, and reports exactly how the run ended.
purpose: Lets a person hand off open-ended or heavy work and get back a checked result within a fixed turn and cost bound.
approach: Runs a goal under a turn and cost bound, checks the result against its done-standard, and reports whether it was met, paused or failed.
out_of_scope: Tiny or conversational requests that need no autonomy, and work with no checkable done-standard.
milestones: 1. Every scripted run outcome (met, silent no-op, paused on a human with a decision id, partial or crashed, missing binary) is reported in the common shape on both the subprocess and ACP runners, and no scenario raises. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: The full agent is the right tool for open-ended work and wasteful for a small edit, so cheap rungs are tried first and verified, with escalation on failure. The two full runners tie on the contract. Cost per success is not yet measured because the scenarios script the process edge. A wrong stop loses work, which is why stall review is a separate solution.
measures_of_success: Each scripted outcome (met, silent no-op, paused on a human with a decision id, partial or crashed, missing binary) is reported in the common shape and no scenario raises. The goal contract's met-versus-limit, stop and resume rules hold.
parameters: Goal text with its done-standard, brief, model, maximum turns, working directory, binary or agent command, timeout, a per-call context preamble and the ordered runner ladder.
inputs: A goal, a brief with gathered context, and optional progress emitter and run identifier for tagging retries.
outputs: A result stating whether the goal was met, the output text, and error or pause details such as a decision id.
effects: Spawns worker processes, edits files or calls operations on the runner's behalf, spends tokens, and emits execution progress events.
usage_notes: Order the ladder from cheapest to most capable and let the verifier decide whether to escalate. Pass a stable run identifier across retries. A runner must never raise.

name: Bounded reversible file writer
description: Gives an automated agent a bounded way to write files in one folder, where each overwrite keeps a readable backup and nothing outside the folder can change.
purpose: Help an automated agent make the file changes a person asked for, inside one folder, without an unrecoverable mistake.
approach: Confine every write to one configured root and keep a recoverable copy before any overwrite.
out_of_scope: Changing binary files or files with secret-like names, which are refused whatever the path.
milestones: 1. Every boundary case (traversal, absolute and sibling-prefix paths, symlink escape, protected names, size and create limits) is refused with the outside untouched, and ordinary writes succeed, on the offline scratch-tree cases. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Containment must resolve symlinks and parent references before testing the boundary, and the read side and write side should share one implementation. Backups belong outside the corpus rather than relying on version control. The binary-extension and secret-name lists are fixed in code, and concurrent writers are not covered.
measures_of_success: All boundary cases (traversal, absolute and sibling-prefix paths, symlink escape, protected names, size and create limits) are refused with the outside untouched, ordinary writes succeed, and an overwrite leaves a readable backup. Standing conditions: Guarantee no write lands outside the configured root and every overwrite keeps a recoverable copy. Refuse oversize, protected and out-of-policy writes without side effects.
parameters: Root directory, backup directory, whether backups are enabled, whether creating new files is allowed, and the maximum bytes per write.
inputs: A path relative to the root and the full replacement content; a read request for the current content.
outputs: A write result stating success, whether the file was created, bytes written, where the backup went and any error; the current text on read.
effects: Creates or replaces a file under the root and writes a backup copy outside it. Nothing changes when the result is not ok.
usage_notes: Constructing the writer is the act of granting write access, so wire it only deliberately. Handle a refused result as an ordinary outcome and escalate rather than retry around it.

name: Allowlisted operation writer
description: A write path to external tool servers that stays separate from reading, so being readable grants nothing and every attempted write is auditable.
purpose: Carry out one named change on an external tool server, and only when an explicit allowlist permits that operation.
approach: Permit a write to an external tool server only when it is on the write allowlist, and run it once with the exact arguments given.
out_of_scope: Reads from a tool server, and any operation that is not on the write allowlist.
milestones: 1. Allowlist cases passed by the write adapter: 15 of 15, with every refused operation making zero server calls. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. Allowed writes run once with exact arguments on a live MCP server, recorded on the same cases.
knowledge: A write allowlist is separate from any read allowlist, so being readable grants nothing here. A refused operation must never touch the server. Names are alias-prefixed so servers do not collide, and the planner may pass the prefixed or bare form. Real servers are not exercised in the offline arm.
measures_of_success: An allowed call reaches the client once with exact arguments, a disallowed call makes zero server calls, and server errors and dead connections come back as failed results with details recorded. Standing conditions: Guarantee that exactly the requested mutation runs once, and that anything off the allowlist is refused with no server call. Make every attempt auditable.
parameters: Server alias and connection spec, the write allowlist of tool names, and the timeout.
inputs: An operation name (prefixed or bare) and its arguments; a discovery call for the writable catalogue.
outputs: A write result with success, error and an audit detail of the tool, arguments and whether it executed; a list of writable operations with schemas.
effects: One mutating call on the external server when allowed; no effect when refused.
usage_notes: List writable operations first, pick at most one, and escalate when refused or failed. Keep the write allowlist narrower than the read one.

name: World: doing things outside the host through the best harness, with declared reach and receipts
description: Does the AI's work outside the host's own data (in a workspace, on external tool servers, on other machines, with people on other channels) through the agent harness that scores best on a combined metric, the coding agent today or an open-source harness, answers every capability question from one declared inventory, and returns every outside act with a receipt of what actually ran.
purpose: Gets real work done in the world for people, at the best balance of results, cost and safety, and lets them trust what the AI says it can do and did.
approach: Carries out outside work through the harness configuration the combined metric ranks best, grounds every claim of reach in a declared inventory, and backs every claim of an outside act with a receipt.
out_of_scope: The goal loop, liveness review and outcome reporting around a deep run, which keep their own specifications; knowledge about the world; and changes to the host's own data.
milestones: 1. A small labelled set exists of outside goals, capability questions, out-of-reach requests, setting-blocked claims and claimed acts, and coding_agent_prompt_reach has a recorded combined score on it. 2. Several open-source agent harnesses have recorded combined scores on the same set, and the best of them is the best_open_source_harness arm. 3. The configuration with the best combined score is selected, whether it keeps the coding agent or replaces it.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner corrected an earlier view that the world was only a role tag over existing solutions: it needs its own specification. What exists: a host-supplied reach summary and a stronger-tier reach judge before planning (core/reach_judge.py, off by default), which on cheap-model routing helped most because it asks a fact rather than reviewing a decision; the tool catalog's when-to-use text; the answer check that flags claims of unexecuted work. Open for the owner: whether conversations with other people inside the host belong to the world. Recorded here as yes, because another person's words carry their own consent and scope and lie outside this request's own data; the other reading (the host's own chat is the body's) changes only which solution owns them. The specification owner's direction (2026-10-28): an option to replace the coding agent for doing things in the world with the best open-source harness chosen by a metric, compared with the coding agent, where the metric combines several things. Each implementation is therefore a whole configuration (a harness and a way of declaring reach), ranked by one combined metric.
measures_of_success: Outside goals are met to their done-standard at a cost and time no worse than the coding agent's; capability answers match the inventory; a blocker is stated only after the setting that causes it was read; every claimed outside act has a receipt. Standing conditions: Never describe a capability the inventory does not hold. Never write outside the boundary or read across scope, whatever the harness.
parameters: The harness, the inventory source, which effectors are wired, whether the reach judge runs and on which tier, and the weights of the combined metric.
inputs: The request, the host's inventory of environments and tools with what each allows, and each effector's result.
outputs: A reach verdict for the request (inside, outside, in the world now, or not reachable, with why), and receipts for outside acts (what ran, where, its id).
effects: Reads the inventory; at most one small model call for the reach verdict; no outside act of its own.
usage_notes: Selected today: coding_agent_prompt_reach. The proposal is best_open_source_harness, compared with the coding agent on the same cases; deep runs keep their goal loop and reporting (run-deep-work) whichever harness runs them.

name: Goal assignee and doability judge
description: Decides the verdicts on who a new goal belongs to and whether an AI representative can take it over, with a model call that is kept only while its measured value outweighs its cost and time.
purpose: Gives a person the verdicts on who a new goal belongs to and whether an AI representative can take it over at a cost and delay that its metric accepts.
approach: A prompt declared as a prompt spec makes one model call to decide who a new goal belongs to and whether an AI can take it over.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier (choose-a-model-tier) and the surrounding turn or run.
milestones: 1. Its metric has a case set and a recorded result for the current arm and the no-model floor. 2. The model call stays only while it beats the floor on the metric.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 so that this prompt has a solution and a metric that justify its cost, time and value; not built, so the metric is unmeasured and the current call is a direction, not a measured win.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from the cases without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Add no time before a chat reply.
parameters: The model tier and any cap the module states.
inputs: The text or events the call is given.
outputs: The text or verdict the call returns.
effects: One model call; no write beyond the text it returns.
usage_notes: Selected today: model_judge. The floor is a proposed arm with no model call. Decision teamdec_f95b130faacd (cases relabelled).
